app.title: BioInterface — Assay Library and Run Workbench
app.summary: A person finds an assay in a structured library by filtering on product type, difficulty, workbench and instrument, or by keyword search, and can compare several side by side on robot time, throughput and step counts. They open one assay's dossier to read its numbered robot steps with the manual analyst steps marked, its deck layout, reagents, acceptance criteria and regulatory references. A four-step wizard then takes the chosen assay (or a protocol typed in plain English) through deck choice and deployment context to a run summary, where they simulate the run or download executable robot code in one of several formats. After the run they upload the instrument's output file, which is parsed and checked against the assay's acceptance criteria to give a per-sample and whole-run pass or fail.

task.text: Choose an assay from a machine-readable library, turn it into an executable automated run, and check the run's output against the assay's acceptance criteria.

data.text: A library of assay protocols stored as structured records (steps, deck layout, instruments, reagents, timings, acceptance criteria), plus instrument output files from completed runs.
data.item: an assay protocol with its ordered robot steps and acceptance criteria

stage.text: planning automated assay runs from a protocol library, then checking the run output against acceptance criteria

mechanism.text: A sidebar switches between modes and sections, and a field selector there reloads the library every view reads from. Filtered tables and side-by-side charts lead to a tabbed detail view of one assay; a stepwise wizard carries the chosen assay into code export, and an upload view evaluates parsed results against that assay's criteria.

field.text: laboratory automation of analytical assays for biopharma QC

workflow.name: pick a protocol from a library, compile it into a run, and check the results against its criteria

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Multiselect filters by product type, difficulty, workbench, instrument used (all must be present) and organism, or a keyword search across name, purpose, reagents, instruments and environment
Pick two or more assays to see a table of robot minutes, throughput, sample volume and step counts, bar charts by difficulty, and a normalised radar chart
Assay Detail shows an autonomy-level badge, key metrics and tabs for robot steps (analyst steps highlighted), deck layout, instruments and reagents, acceptance criteria and regulatory references

steps.step: lay out the run step by step
steps.here: A four-step wizard: pick a library assay or parse a plain-English protocol, choose a saved deck or placeholders, choose a deployment context (manual, robotic arm, rail robot, scheduler), then review a run summary and pipeline preview
Download the run as PyLabRobot, UniteLabs, Rail System or Opentrons Python, or as an execution-plan JSON; or simulate the run, or save it as a template
Choose a completed pipeline run, drop the instrument output file; its format is detected and parsed into per-sample measurements

Each sample's measurements are checked against the assay's acceptance criteria, giving a per-sample verdict table, a card per criterion with rule and measured value, and a whole-run pass, fail or partial badge

distinctive: Each protocol separates steps a robot runs from steps where an analyst must intervene, and these are counted and highlighted throughout
The same protocol compiles to several robot code targets, and the deployment context changes how plate transfers between instruments are inserted
Each assay carries an autonomy level saying how far a robot can run it today
Acceptance criteria travel with the protocol, so uploaded results are judged against the rules of the assay that was run
Instrument output from several plate readers and QC instruments is recognised by format and parsed automatically
